content: 1. Saccharomyces boulardii can be administered as one capsule or packet orally twice daily. The capsule may be swallowed whole, or its contents can be emptied onto the tongue and followed by drinking 4 ounces of water or juice. Alternatively, the capsule or packet can be opened and sprinkled over semi-solid food, such as applesauce or yogurt. The contents may also be dissolved in liquids like water, juice, or milk before consumption. 2. Saccharomyces boulardii is indicated for the restoration of intestinal flora, the treatment of post-antibiotic diarrhea, and the prevention of post-antibiotic vulvovaginal candidiasis. 3. Amphotericin B cholesteryl sulfate reduces the effects of Saccharomyces boulardii through an unspecified interaction mechanism. It is recommended to avoid or use an alternative drug. Systemic or oral antifungals may decrease the activity of this probiotic. 4. Patients with a central line, yeast allergy, or hypersensitivity to the product or its excipients should not use Saccharomyces boulardii. Caution is advised in patients with lactose intolerance, as some formulations may contain lactose. Immunocompromised patients should also use this product with caution, as it contains live bacteria, and cases of fungemia have been reported in premature infants. 21. Packets or capsules should not be opened near patients with central lines. Gloves should be changed after handling the product to prevent accidental transfer into central lines. 22. Dietary supplements, including Saccharomyces boulardii, are not reviewed by the FDA for safety or efficacy. There is insufficient conclusive evidence to support the widespread use of this product for the treatment of diarrhea. 23. Potentially significant drug interactions may occur. Monitoring, dose adjustments, or alternative therapies may be necessary. 24. The safety of Saccharomyces boulardii during pregnancy and lactation is not well established. It is unknown if the product is excreted into breast milk. Pregnant or breastfeeding patients should consult a healthcare professional before using over-the-counter medications. 25. Pregnancy Category A: Controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk.
